<!-- B"H
Boruch Hashem
Blessed is He

The Awtsmoos creates critique and correction in the same instant; Awtsmoos.com lets each objection polish the vessel until transport, domain truth, and user experience rhyme without accident.
-->
# Critique — Twenty-Four Improvements

1. Do not globally infer HTTP status from arbitrary domain objects.
2. Do not throw for expected validation failures when handlers already return structured bodies.
3. Preserve every existing JSON field exactly.
4. Keep successful `/` and `/status` HTTP 200.
5. Keep successful create/task HTTP 200.
6. Use the framework-supported envelope rather than hand-inventing a response protocol.
7. Hide the framework dependency behind an Olam-local adapter.
8. Give the adapter one responsibility: transport manifestation.
9. Default absent/invalid body status to 200 only for successful bodies.
10. Accept only legal HTTP status values before passing transport metadata.
11. Ensure headers remain no-store JSON.
12. Prove normalization recognizes the adapter output as wrapped.
13. Prove the sender sets Node response status.
14. Prove response body still parses to the original object.
15. Preserve browser `data.ok === false` behavior.
16. Preserve requestId/type metadata.
17. Do not touch MiniMax provider payload mapping.
18. Do not touch image replacement code already proven correct.
19. Re-run 43+ deterministic tests after the change.
20. Re-probe the real public endpoints after deployment.
21. Re-run the public five-browser UI suites after deployment.
22. Re-fetch remote before commit and before push because other agents are active.
23. Never deploy an older SHA over unrelated newer production; integrate onto latest remote lineage.
24. Keep all new/rewritten source under 120 lines with tabs and full Awtsmoos documentation.
